This vignette compares `pyfixest` with R's `fixest`: first a side-by-side syntax reference, then intentional formula differences, and finally numerical comparisons via the `rpy2` package.

## Syntax comparison

The tables below map common `fixest` syntax to `pyfixest` (assuming `import pyfixest as pf` in Python, `library(fixest)` in R, and a DataFrame `dat`). For a Stata-oriented reference, see [Translating Stata to PyFixest](../how-to/stata-2-pyfixest.qmd); for deeper formula details, see [Formula Syntax](../tutorials/formula-syntax.qmd).

Two general differences apply across the tables:

- **Default standard errors**: Unlike `fixest` (which clusters on the first fixed effect by default), `pyfixest` defaults to `"iid"` standard errors even when fixed effects are present. Pass `vcov={"CRV1": "..."}` explicitly to cluster.
- **Unimplemented formula shortcuts**: Where `fixest` offers formula-level macros (`.[ctrls]`), regex wildcards (`..(...)`), or panel operators (`l()`, `f()`, `d()`), `pyfixest` relies on standard Python f-strings, list comprehensions, and pandas/polars DataFrame transforms.

### Models

| Task | `pyfixest` | `fixest` |
|---|---|---|
| Simple OLS | `pf.feols("wage ~ educ + age", data=dat)` | `feols(wage ~ educ + age, data = dat)` |
| Categorical regressor | `pf.feols("wage ~ educ + i(treat)", data=dat)` (or `C(treat)`) | `feols(wage ~ educ + i(treat), data = dat)` |
| Categorical regressor (reference level) | `pf.feols("wage ~ educ + i(treat, ref=1)", data=dat)` | `feols(wage ~ educ + i(treat, ref = 1), data = dat)` |
| Fixed effects (iid SEs) | `pf.feols("wage ~ educ | countyfips", data=dat)` | `feols(wage ~ educ | countyfips, data = dat, vcov = "iid")` |
| Fixed effects (clustered SEs) | `pf.feols("wage ~ educ | countyfips", data=dat, vcov={"CRV1": "countyfips"})` | `feols(wage ~ educ | countyfips, data = dat)` |
| Observation weights | `pf.feols("wage ~ educ + i(treat)", data=dat, weights="w")` | `feols(wage ~ educ + i(treat), data = dat, weights = ~w)` |
| Instrumental variables (2SLS) | `pf.feols("wage ~ marr + [educ ~ age] | countyfips", data=dat)` | `feols(wage ~ marr | countyfips | educ ~ age, data = dat)` |
| Nonlinear model (Logit / Probit) | `pf.feglm("marr ~ age + black + hisp", data=dat, family="logit")` | `feglm(marr ~ age + black + hisp, data = dat, family = "logit")` |
| Nonlinear model (Poisson) | `pf.fepois("count_y ~ age + black + hisp | statefips + year", data=dat, vcov={"CRV1": "statefips"})` | `fepois(count_y ~ age + black + hisp | statefips + year, data = dat)` |
| Sample split | `pf.feols("wage ~ educ | countyfips", data=dat, split="hisp")` (or `fsplit="hisp"`) | `feols(wage ~ educ | countyfips, data = dat, split = ~hisp)` (or `fsplit = ~hisp`) |
| Multiple dependent variables | `pf.feols("sw(wage, educ) ~ age + marr | countyfips + year", data=dat)` | `feols(c(wage, educ) ~ age + marr | countyfips + year, data = dat)` |
| Stepwise estimation | `pf.feols("wage ~ educ + sw(age, marr)", data=dat)` (also `sw0`, `mvsw`) | `feols(wage ~ educ + sw(age, marr), data = dat)` (also `sw0`, `mvsw`) |
| Cumulative stepwise estimation | `pf.feols("wage ~ educ + csw(age, marr)", data=dat)` (also `csw0`) | `feols(wage ~ educ + csw(age, marr), data = dat)` (also `csw0`) |
| Cumulative stepwise fixed effects | `pf.feols("wage ~ educ | csw(year, statefips)", data=dat)` | `feols(wage ~ educ | csw(year, statefips), data = dat)` |
| Macros (emulated via f-string) | `ctrls = ["age", "black", "hisp", "marr"]`<br>`pf.feols(f"wage ~ educ + {' + '.join(ctrls)}", data=dat)` | `ctrls = c("age", "black", "hisp", "marr")`<br>`feols(wage ~ educ + .[ctrls], data = dat)` |
| Wildcards: starts with (emulated) | `pf.feols(f"wage ~ educ + {' + '.join(c for c in dat.columns if c.startswith('x'))}", data=dat)` | `feols(wage ~ educ + ..("^x"), data = dat)` |
| Wildcards: ends with (emulated) | `pf.feols(f"wage ~ educ + {' + '.join(c for c in dat.columns if c.endswith('sp'))}", data=dat)` | `feols(wage ~ educ + ..("sp$"), data = dat)` |
| Wildcards: contains (emulated) | `pf.feols(f"wage ~ educ + {' + '.join(c for c in dat.columns if 'ac' in c)}", data=dat)` | `feols(wage ~ educ + ..("ac"), data = dat)` |

### Interactions

| Task | `pyfixest` | `fixest` |
|---|---|---|
| Continuous × continuous (interaction only) | `pf.feols("wage ~ educ:age", data=dat)` | `feols(wage ~ educ:age, data = dat)` |
| Continuous × continuous (full) | `pf.feols("wage ~ educ*age", data=dat)` | `feols(wage ~ educ*age, data = dat)` |
| Polynomial (single term) | `pf.feols("wage ~ I(age**2)", data=dat)` | `feols(wage ~ I(age^2), data = dat)` |
| Polynomial (full) | `pf.feols("wage ~ age + I(age**2)", data=dat)` (or `poly(age, degree=2, raw=True)`) | `feols(wage ~ poly(age, 2, raw = TRUE), data = dat)` |
| Categorical × categorical (cells) | `pf.feols("wage ~ i(treat, C(hisp))", data=dat)` | `feols(wage ~ i(treat, i.hisp), data = dat)` |
| Categorical × categorical (nested) | `pf.feols("wage ~ C(treat)/C(hisp)", data=dat)` | `feols(wage ~ factor(treat)/factor(hisp), data = dat)` |
| Categorical × categorical (full) | `pf.feols("wage ~ C(treat)*C(hisp)", data=dat)` | `feols(wage ~ factor(treat)*factor(hisp), data = dat)` |
| Categorical × continuous (slopes only) | `pf.feols("wage ~ i(treat, age)", data=dat)` (or `C(treat):age`) | `feols(wage ~ i(treat, age), data = dat)` (or `factor(treat):age`) |
| Categorical × continuous (nested) | `pf.feols("wage ~ C(treat)/age", data=dat)` | `feols(wage ~ factor(treat)/age, data = dat)` |
| Categorical × continuous (full) | `pf.feols("wage ~ C(treat)*age", data=dat)` | `feols(wage ~ factor(treat)*age, data = dat)` |
| Interacted fixed effects | `pf.feols("wage ~ educ | statefips:year", data=dat)` | `feols(wage ~ educ | statefips^year, data = dat)` |
| Varying slopes (with level intercepts) | `pf.feols("wage ~ educ | statefips[year]", data=dat)` | `feols(wage ~ educ | statefips[year], data = dat)` |
| Varying slopes (slopes only) | `pf.feols("wage ~ educ | statefips[[year]]", data=dat)` | `feols(wage ~ educ | statefips[[year]], data = dat)` |

In `pyfixest`, a numeric second variable in `i(treat, hisp)` is treated as continuous unless wrapped in `C()` (unlike `fixest`'s `i.hisp` prefix), and arithmetic powers inside `I(...)` use Python's `**` operator (see [Covariate powers](#covariate-powers) below).

### Standard errors

| Task | `pyfixest` | `fixest` |
|---|---|---|
| IID | `pf.feols("wage ~ educ", data=dat, vcov="iid")` (default) | `feols(wage ~ educ, data = dat, vcov = "iid")` |
| Heteroskedasticity-robust (HC1) | `pf.feols("wage ~ educ", data=dat, vcov="HC1")` (or `"hetero"`) | `feols(wage ~ educ, data = dat, vcov = "HC1")` (or `"hetero"`) |
| Heteroskedasticity-robust (HC3) | `pf.feols("wage ~ educ", data=dat, vcov="HC3")` (without absorbed FE) | `feols(wage ~ educ, data = dat, vcov = sandwich::vcovHC)` |
| HAC (Newey-West) | `pf.feols("wage ~ educ", data=dat, vcov="NW", vcov_kwargs={"time_id": "year", "panel_id": "unit"})` | `feols(wage ~ educ, data = dat, vcov = "NW", panel.id = ~unit + year)` |
| HAC (Driscoll-Kraay) | `pf.feols("wage ~ educ", data=dat, vcov="DK", vcov_kwargs={"time_id": "year", "panel_id": "unit"})` | `feols(wage ~ educ, data = dat, vcov = "DK", panel.id = ~unit + year)` |
| One-way clustered | `pf.feols("wage ~ educ | countyfips", data=dat, vcov={"CRV1": "countyfips"})` | `feols(wage ~ educ | countyfips, data = dat, vcov = ~countyfips)` |
| Two-way clustered | `pf.feols("wage ~ educ | countyfips + year", data=dat, vcov={"CRV1": "countyfips + year"})` | `feols(wage ~ educ | countyfips + year, data = dat, vcov = ~countyfips + year)` |
| Interacted clustering (emulated) | `pf.feols("wage ~ educ | countyfips:year", data=dat.assign(cy=dat["countyfips"].astype(str) + "_" + dat["year"].astype(str)), vcov={"CRV1": "cy"})` | `feols(wage ~ educ | countyfips^year, data = dat, vcov = ~countyfips^year)` |
| Conley spatial SEs | Not supported | `feols(wage ~ educ, data = dat, vcov = conley("25 mi"))` |

For time-series Newey-West standard errors without a panel dimension, omit `"panel_id"` from `vcov_kwargs`; pass `"lag"` to set the lag length explicitly.

### Panel

`pyfixest` does not yet provide built-in formula panel operators (`l()`, `f()`, `d()`). Instead, sort the DataFrame by unit and period (`dat = dat.sort_values(["unit", "year"])`) and construct lagged, lead, or differenced columns before estimation:

| Task | `pyfixest` (emulated via pandas) | `fixest` |
|---|---|---|
| Lag (1 period) | `dat["wage_l1"] = dat.groupby("unit")["wage"].shift(1)`<br>`pf.feols("wage ~ educ + wage_l1", data=dat)` | `feols(wage ~ educ + l(wage, 1), data = dat, panel.id = ~unit + year)` |
| Lead (1 period) | `dat["wage_f1"] = dat.groupby("unit")["wage"].shift(-1)`<br>`pf.feols("wage ~ educ + wage_f1", data=dat)` | `feols(wage ~ educ + f(wage, 1), data = dat, panel.id = ~unit + year)` |
| First difference | `dat["wage_d1"] = dat.groupby("unit")["wage"].diff()`<br>`pf.feols("wage ~ educ + wage_d1", data=dat)` | `feols(wage ~ educ + d(wage), data = dat, panel.id = ~unit + year)` |

These `.shift()` and `.diff()` expressions assume contiguous periods within each unit; if a panel has time gaps, reindex the time grid before shifting.

## Intentional formula differences

### Covariate powers

For covariates, PyFixest prioritizes
[Formulaic's formula conventions](https://matthew.wardrop.casa/formulaic/latest/guides/grammar/)
over `fixest`'s arithmetic-power convention. Outside a Python expression such
as `I(...)`, both `^` and `**` expand interactions up to the specified order:

| Covariate formula | PyFixest interpretation |
|---|---|
| `Y ~ X1 + X1^2` | `Y ~ X1`; no squared term is added |
| `Y ~ X1 + X1**2` | `Y ~ X1`; no squared term is added |
| `Y ~ (X1 + X2)^2` | `Y ~ X1 + X2 + X1:X2` |
| `Y ~ (X1 + X2)**2` | `Y ~ X1 + X2 + X1:X2` |

In particular, a single-factor power such as `X1^2` reduces to `X1` under
these formula rules. It does **not** square the values of `X1`, and adding it
alongside `X1` has no effect. This also applies when the model has fixed effects.
In contrast, `fixest` 0.14.0 interprets covariate `X1^2` as the arithmetic
transformation `I(X1^2)`, and `(X1 + X2)^2` as `I((X1 + X2)^2)`.
This is an intentional syntax difference; see
[#1765](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/issues/1765).

To include an arithmetic square in PyFixest, use `I(X1**2)`:

```python
import pyfixest as pf

data = pf.get_data()
fit_squared = pf.feols("Y ~ X1 + I(X1**2)", data=data)
fit_squared_fe = pf.feols("Y ~ X1 + I(X1**2) | f1", data=data)
```

Inside `I(...)`, expressions follow Python arithmetic: `**`
means exponentiation, while `^` means bitwise XOR. Use `I(X1**2)` when
translating R's `I(X1^2)`.

## Setup


```{python}
import pandas as pd
import rpy2.robjects as ro
from rpy2.robjects import numpy2ri, pandas2ri
from rpy2.robjects.conversion import Converter
from rpy2.robjects.packages import importr
from rpy2.robjects.vectors import ListVector
from rpy2.rinterface import ListSexpVector

import pyfixest as pf

# Import R packages
fixest = importr("fixest")
stats = importr("stats")
broom = importr("broom")

# Enable automatic pandas <-> R DataFrame conversion (rpy2 >= 3.6)
# Keep R list classes intact (avoid conversion to NamedList).
_list_guard = Converter("pandas2ri-list-guard")

@_list_guard.rpy2py.register(ListSexpVector)
def _keep_r_list_classes(obj):
    return ListVector(obj)

_converter_ctx = (
    ro.default_converter + numpy2ri.converter + pandas2ri.converter + _list_guard
).context()
_converter_ctx.__enter__()

# IPython magic commands for autoreloading
%load_ext autoreload
%autoreload 2

# Get data using pyfixest
data = pf.get_data(model="Feols", N=10_000, seed=99292)
```


## Ordinary Least Squares (OLS)

### IID Inference

First, we estimate a model via `pyfixest. We compute "iid" standard errors.


```{python}
fit = pf.feols(fml="Y ~ X1 + X2 | f1 + f2", data=data, vcov="iid")
```

We estimate the same model with weights:


```{python}
fit_weights = pf.feols(
    fml="Y ~ X1 + X2 | f1 + f2", data=data, weights="weights", vcov="iid"
)
```

Via `r-fixest` and `rpy2`, we get


```{python}
r_fit = fixest.feols(
    ro.Formula("Y ~ X1 + X2 | f1 + f2"),
    data=data,
    vcov="iid",
)

r_fit_weights = fixest.feols(
    ro.Formula("Y ~ X1 + X2 | f1 + f2"),
    data=data,
    weights=ro.Formula("~weights"),
    vcov="iid",
)
```

    R[write to console]: NOTE: 3 observations removed because of NA values (LHS: 1, RHS: 1, Fixed-effects: 1).

    R[write to console]: NOTE: 3 observations removed because of NA values (LHS: 1, RHS: 1, Fixed-effects: 1).



Let's compare how close the covariance matrices are:


```{python}
fit_vcov = fit.variance_covariance.vcov
r_vcov = stats.vcov(r_fit)
fit_vcov - r_vcov
```


And for WLS:


```{python}
fit_weights.variance_covariance.vcov - stats.vcov(r_fit_weights)
```

We conclude by comparing all estimation results via the `tidy` methods:

```{python}
fit.tidy()
```

```{python}
pd.DataFrame(broom.tidy_fixest(r_fit)).T
```

```{python}
fit_weights.tidy()
```

```{python}
pd.DataFrame(broom.tidy_fixest(r_fit_weights)).T
```


### Heteroskedastic Errors

We repeat the same exercise with heteroskedastic (HC1) errors:


```{python}
fit = pf.feols(fml="Y ~ X1 + X2 | f1 + f2", data=data, vcov="hetero")
fit_weights = pf.feols(
    fml="Y ~ X1 + X2 | f1 + f2", data=data, vcov="hetero", weights="weights"
)
```


```{python}
r_fit = fixest.feols(
    ro.Formula("Y ~ X1 + X2 | f1 + f2"),
    data=data,
    vcov="hetero",
)

r_fit_weights = fixest.feols(
    ro.Formula("Y ~ X1 + X2 | f1 + f2"),
    data=data,
    weights=ro.Formula("~weights"),
    vcov="hetero",
)
```

As before, we compare the variance covariance matrices:


```{python}
fit.variance_covariance.vcov - stats.vcov(r_fit)
```

```{python}
fit_weights.variance_covariance.vcov - stats.vcov(r_fit_weights)
```

We conclude by comparing all estimation results via the `tidy` methods:

```{python}
fit.tidy()
```

```{python}
pd.DataFrame(broom.tidy_fixest(r_fit)).T
```

```{python}
fit_weights.tidy()
```

```{python}
pd.DataFrame(broom.tidy_fixest(r_fit_weights)).T
```


### Cluster-Robust Errors

We conclude with cluster robust errors.


```{python}
fit = pf.feols(fml="Y ~ X1 + X2 | f1 + f2", data=data, vcov={"CRV1": "f1"})
fit_weights = pf.feols(
    fml="Y ~ X1 + X2 | f1 + f2", data=data, vcov={"CRV1": "f1"}, weights="weights"
)

r_fit = fixest.feols(
    ro.Formula("Y ~ X1 + X2 | f1 + f2"),
    data=data,
    vcov=ro.Formula("~f1"),
)
r_fit_weights = fixest.feols(
    ro.Formula("Y ~ X1 + X2 | f1 + f2"),
    data=data,
    weights=ro.Formula("~weights"),
    vcov=ro.Formula("~f1"),
)
```

```{python}
fit.variance_covariance.vcov - stats.vcov(r_fit)
```

```{python}
fit_weights.variance_covariance.vcov - stats.vcov(r_fit_weights)
```

We conclude by comparing all estimation results via the `tidy` methods:

```{python}
fit.tidy()
```

```{python}
pd.DataFrame(broom.tidy_fixest(r_fit)).T
```

```{python}
fit_weights.tidy()
```

```{python}
pd.DataFrame(broom.tidy_fixest(r_fit_weights)).T
```

## Poisson Regression


```{python}
data = pf.get_data(model="Fepois")
```


```{python}
fit_iid = pf.fepois(fml="Y ~ X1 + X2 | f1 + f2", data=data, vcov="iid", iwls_tol=1e-10)
fit_hetero = pf.fepois(
    fml="Y ~ X1 + X2 | f1 + f2", data=data, vcov="hetero", iwls_tol=1e-10
)
fit_crv = pf.fepois(
    fml="Y ~ X1 + X2 | f1 + f2", data=data, vcov={"CRV1": "f1"}, iwls_tol=1e-10
)

fit_r_iid = fixest.fepois(
    ro.Formula("Y ~ X1 + X2 | f1 + f2"),
    data=data,
    vcov="iid",
)

fit_r_hetero = fixest.fepois(
    ro.Formula("Y ~ X1 + X2 | f1 + f2"),
    data=data,
    vcov="hetero",
)

fit_r_crv = fixest.fepois(
    ro.Formula("Y ~ X1 + X2 | f1 + f2"),
    data=data,
    vcov=ro.Formula("~f1"),
)
```

```{python}
fit_iid.variance_covariance.vcov - stats.vcov(fit_r_iid)
```

```{python}
fit_hetero.variance_covariance.vcov - stats.vcov(fit_r_hetero)
```

```{python}
fit_crv.variance_covariance.vcov - stats.vcov(fit_r_crv)
```

We conclude by comparing all estimation results via the `tidy` methods:


```{python}
fit_iid.tidy()
```

```{python}
pd.DataFrame(broom.tidy_fixest(fit_r_iid)).T
```

```{python}
fit_hetero.tidy()
```

```{python}
pd.DataFrame(broom.tidy_fixest(fit_r_hetero)).T
```

```{python}
fit_crv.tidy()
```

```{python}
pd.DataFrame(broom.tidy_fixest(fit_r_crv)).T
```
